info.name: ReSolve API
info.description:
Complete collection of API routes for the ReSolve application.

## Auto Token Management
The Login request automatically saves the access token as a collection variable. All authenticated requests use it via the collection-level pre-request script — no manual copy-paste needed.

## Quick Start
1. Create the owner account once with `bun run seed` (there is no register endpoint)
2. Login with your OWNER_EMAIL / OWNER_PASSWORD (tokens are auto-saved)
3. All subsequent requests automatically include the token
4. Logout invalidates the refresh token and clears both cookies

`baseUrl` assumes PORT=6000, matching .env.example.

exec: // Auto-inject Authorization header for every request

item.name: Auth
item.description: Authentication endpoints. Login auto-saves the tokens; Logout clears them and the cookies. There is no register endpoint — see `bun run seed`.

request.description: Use the OWNER_EMAIL / OWNER_PASSWORD from your .env — the account created by `bun run seed`. Saves both tokens as collection variables.

exec: // Auto-save tokens so you never have to copy-paste
console.log('✅ accessToken saved to collection variables');
console.log('✅ refreshToken saved to collection variables');

request.description: Uses the refreshToken cookie (set automatically by the Login response) to get a new accessToken.
Deletes the refresh token row and clears the accessToken/refreshToken cookies. Reads the refreshToken cookie set by Login — no Authorization header required.

exec: // The server clears both cookies with the same attributes it set
// them with, so the jar should come back empty for both names.
// Drop the saved tokens so later requests don't send a dead one
console.log('\u2705 tokens cleared from collection variables');

item.name: Users
item.description: Profile management for the single owner account.

request.description: Requires auth. Returns the logged-in user's profile.
Requires auth. Updates the logged-in user's profile.

item.name: Problems
item.description: Capture problems from a LeetCode URL or create custom ones, then browse, filter, and edit the library. Capture is one endpoint discriminated on `source`.

request.description: Resolves title, difficulty, and topics for a LeetCode URL without saving anything. Responds 200 with the resolved metadata, or 422 (echoing the canonical URL) when the lookup fails. If the canonical URL is already saved, the response carries `existingProblemId` so the client can open it instead of creating a duplicate.

exec: // Already in the library? Keep the id so the follow-up
// requests address the existing record instead of
console.log('✅ problemId saved from existing record:', data.existingProblemId);

request.description: Canonicalizes the URL (query strings and trailing segments like /description or /solutions are discarded), resolves metadata from LeetCode, and saves. Responds 201 on create, or 200 with `alreadyExisted: true` when the canonical URL is already in the library. Saves `problemId`.

The fallback for when metadata resolution fails or returns 422: supply title, difficulty, and topics alongside the URL and no external lookup happens. The record is flagged `metadataEnteredManually: true`. `UNRATED` is not accepted for a LeetCode problem.

body.raw:
{
    "source": "CUSTOM",
    "title": "Rotate a matrix in place",
    "difficulty": "MEDIUM",
    "topics": [
        "array",
        "matrix"
    ],
    "sourceName": "Cracking the Coding Interview",
    "sourceUrl": "https://example.com/ch1",
    "statement": "Rotate an N x N matrix 90 degrees clockwise without allocating a second matrix."
}

request.description: A problem from an interview, course, book, or self-authored. Only `title` is required; difficulty defaults to `UNRATED`. `sourceUrl` must be an absolute http(s) URL. Custom problems are first-class: identical attempt, scheduling, dashboard, and insights behavior.
Paginated library listing, newest-first by default. Meta carries page, limit, total, and totalPages.

Filters combine conjunctively. `difficulty`, `status`, `topic`, and `pattern` accept comma-separated lists and match any supplied value. `status` accepts SCHEDULED, DUE, OVERDUE, MASTERED, NEEDS_REINFORCEMENT — the first three are evaluated against today in the owner timezone, and problems with no revision cycle are excluded. `hasRecallCard=false` is the “attempted but never written up” backlog. `search` is a case-insensitive title match — use /search to match note and card text. Sort over createdAt, title, difficulty, or nextDueAt.

Full metadata, topics, current stage and due date, practice state, attempt history newest-first, revision event history, and the projected revision timeline (each stage marked completed / current / upcoming). For an unattempted problem the timeline is empty and `cycleStartsOnFirstAttempt` is true.

Corrects title, difficulty, topics, source name/URL, and statement. Supplying `topics` replaces the full set. Changing a LeetCode problem’s canonical URL is rejected with 400, as is `UNRATED` on a LeetCode problem. Editing never disturbs attempts or the revision schedule.

`sourceName`, `sourceUrl`, and `statement` are settable on any problem, not just custom ones. Send `null` for any of the three to clear it — omitting a field leaves it unchanged, so clearing has to be explicit. `sourceUrl` must still be an absolute http(s) URL when non-null.
Removes the problem along with its attempts, topic links, revision schedule, and revision history.

item.name: Attempts
item.description: Logging an attempt is what drives the revision engine. Attempts are append-mostly; edit and delete are deliberate operations that replay the whole schedule.

request.description: Outcome is one of SOLVED_INDEPENDENTLY, SOLVED_WITH_HINT, VIEWED_SOLUTION. Duration is an integer 1–1440 minutes, confidence an integer 1–5, notes optional. `attemptedAt` defaults to now and may be backdated but not future-dated. The response carries the resulting stage and next due date. On a problem with no prior attempts this starts the cycle at DAY_1. Saves `attemptId`.

Run immediately after `Log Attempt` on the same problem. The ladder is DAY_0 → DAY_1 → DAY_3 → DAY_7 → DAY_15 → DAY_30, so completing DAY_1 independently advances to DAY_3, due the anchor plus 3 days. A third independent solve then advances to DAY_7.

Backfilling a session you forgot to log. `attemptedAt` is an ISO timestamp resolved to a local date in the owner timezone, so it is the local day — not the instant — that drives stage arithmetic. A future timestamp responds 400. Because the schedule is replayed from the full history, inserting an attempt earlier than existing ones produces the same result as if it had been logged in order.
A viewed solution resets the cycle to Day 0 at any stage, including after mastery, and permanently marks the problem `solutionViewed`.
A problem’s attempt history, newest-first, with a meta block carrying page, limit, and total.

Correcting a mis-logged attempt. Changing outcome, confidence, or timestamp replays the problem’s schedule from its full attempt history rather than patching it, so the result equals what a fresh log would have produced.
Removes the attempt and replays the schedule. Deleting a problem’s only attempt returns it to having no revision cycle.

item.name: Revisions
item.description: The Day 0/1/3/7/15/30 schedule and its audit trail. Every scheduling transition is recorded as a revision event.

request.description: Revision events newest-first: CYCLE_STARTED, COMPLETED, ADVANCED, REPEATED, RESET, RESCHEDULED, MASTERED, REINFORCEMENT_STARTED — each with its stage, previous and new due dates, any reason, and a UTC timestamp.

Moves the current stage’s due date without changing the stage. The reason is required (whitespace-only is rejected), and a date earlier than today in the owner timezone responds 400. The cycle anchor used for subsequent stages is left untouched, and a RESCHEDULED event records the change.

item.name: Topics
item.description: The normalized topic vocabulary. Topics are created on demand when a problem is tagged — there is no create endpoint.

request.description: Every topic with its problem count, most-used first. Unused topics are returned with a count of 0.
Excludes topics no longer linked to any problem.

Renames a topic, re-deriving its slug. When the new name normalizes to an existing topic’s slug the two are merged: every link moves to the survivor, duplicates collapse to one, and the emptied record is deleted.

item.name: Patterns
item.description: The owner-authored technique vocabulary. Where a topic says what a problem is about, a pattern says how it is solved. Patterns are created on demand when a recall card is written — there is no create endpoint, and they cannot be assigned through the problem payload.

request.description: Every pattern with its problem count, most-used first. Near-duplicate entries show up here as singletons.
Excludes patterns no longer linked to any problem.

Renames a pattern, re-deriving its slug. When the new name normalizes onto an existing pattern the two merge: links move to the survivor, duplicates collapse, and the emptied record is deleted. This is how `two-pointer` and `two-pointers` get collapsed months after both were invented.

item.name: Recall
item.description: The recall layer: the durable knowledge record for a problem, and the pattern-grouped sheet for reviewing technique-by-technique. A card is independent of the attempt log — writing one never touches the revision schedule.

request.description: Creates the card (201) or replaces it (200). Replacement is total: a field omitted here is stored as empty, and an omitted `patterns` list clears the problem's patterns. Saving always advances the card's updatedAt, which is what clears a stale flag.

body.raw:
{
    "keyInsight": "Expand around each centre; a palindrome is symmetric about one index or one gap",
    "approach": "For each i, expand (i, i) and (i, i+1) while the ends match, tracking the longest span.",
    "pitfalls": "Forgetting the even-length centre; off-by-one when slicing the final span.",
    "timeComplexity": "O(n^2)",
    "spaceComplexity": "O(1)",
    "patterns": [
        "Two Pointers",
        "Expand Around Centre"
    ]
}

request.description: The card with its patterns and `needsRecallUpdate`. Responds 404 when the problem has no card yet.
Removes the card and the problem's patterns — patterns are authored as part of the card. Attempts and the revision schedule are untouched.
Every card grouped by pattern — the pre-interview skim. A problem tagged with several patterns appears under each; cards with no pattern land in a trailing untagged group.
Filters by pattern, topic, difficulty, and practice status, combined conjunctively. Status is evaluated against today's date in the owner's timezone.

item.name: Dashboard
item.description: The one question the product answers every day.

request.description: Due and overdue counts, the full ordered due list (most overdue first, then earliest due, then creation time), a recommended slice capped at five, the current practice streak, and a seven-day lookahead starting tomorrow with zero-count days included. All day boundaries use the owner timezone; mastered and never-attempted problems are excluded.

item.name: Insights
item.description: Aggregates computed from stored attempts and revision events, so editing or deleting an attempt changes the reported figures.

request.description: Problems added, attempted, solved independently, and mastered; the revision completion rate with its numerator and denominator (null rate when nothing has come due); and average solve time split into first-attempt and revision buckets with sample counts.
The same figures over a local date range. A start later than the end, malformed dates, or a range beyond the configured maximum all respond 400.

Per-topic problem count, attempt count, independent-solve rate, average confidence, and average solve time, plus a weak-topics list ordered worst-first. A topic below the configured minimum attempt count is reported with its figures but never flagged weak.

Per-pattern solve rate, average confidence, and average solve time, with weak patterns flagged — the same shape and the same configured thresholds as topic insights, over techniques rather than subject areas.
One entry per local date with its attempt count, suitable for a calendar heatmap. Days with no activity are present with a count of 0. Defaults to the trailing 365 days.
The current overdue count plus a trend series giving the overdue count as at the end of each local day, so backlog growth or reduction is visible. Defaults to the trailing 30 days.

item.name: Search
item.description: Cross-entity search over everything the owner has written: problem titles and statements, recall-card fields, attempt notes, and topic and pattern names. Case-insensitive substring matching over a bounded candidate set — `meta.truncated` reports when the cap stopped the scan short.

request.description: Each matching problem is returned once, with the fields that matched and a snippet around each. Results are ordered by the highest-priority field matched: title, pattern, topic, key insight, approach, pitfalls, statement, attempt note.
Restricts matching to the owner's own writing. Scopes: problem, recall, attempt, vocabulary.
Pagination applies within the bounded candidate set.

item.name: Settings
item.description: The single owner’s timezone, notification toggle, and reminder time. The record is created with defaults on first read.

request.description: Creates the record on demand with timezone `UTC`, notifications disabled, and reminder time `20:00` if it does not yet exist.

Accepts any subset of the settable fields; unsupplied fields are unchanged and an empty body is rejected with 400. The timezone must be a valid IANA identifier and governs every local-day computation in the product, taking effect immediately with no data migration. Reminder time is 24-hour `HH:mm`.

item.name: Reminders
item.description: Server-computed reminder state the client polls while the app is open. There is no scheduler and no server-initiated push — closed-browser delivery is out of scope per PRD §6.8.

request.description: Reports `active`, `dueTomorrow`, `dueToday`, `overdueToday`, `reminderTime`, `timezone`, `acknowledged`, the local date it applies to, and a ready-to-render notification title, body, and target path. A reminder becomes active when notifications are enabled, the local time is at or after the reminder time, and at least one problem falls due on the next local date — and stays active for the rest of that local day.

Marks today’s reminder acknowledged so the client does not re-raise a notification or banner for the same day. The acknowledgement is stored as a local date, so it resets by itself when the local date rolls over. Acknowledging while nothing is active responds 200 and leaves the state unchanged.
